title: Exertional Substernal Pressure in Patient with Cardiovascular Risk Factors

history.chief_complaint: Substernal chest tightness provoked by walking up stairs, lasting 10 minutes

examination_findings.physical_exam: Regular rate and rhythm, S1/S2 present without murmur or gallop. Chest wall non-tender to palpation.

lab_results.ecg_12_lead: Sinus rhythm with mild T-wave flattening in V4-V6

expected_followup_questions: Does the chest tightness radiate to your left arm, neck, or jaw?
Do you experience sweating, nausea, or dizziness during episodes?
How long does the discomfort take to resolve after you sit down and rest?
expected_safety_checks: Evaluate cardiovascular medication interactions with Amlodipine and Atorvastatin
Monitor renal parameters before recommending contrast-based imaging
expected_do_not_recommend: High-dose non-selective NSAIDs (e.g. Ibuprofen, Naproxen) without gastroprotective cover
Immediate strenuous physical exertion test prior to outpatient cardiology review
